status: Florensky: two reports, one walkable threshold; all four works retained
summary: What did 180 degrees depend on? Euclid returns to the museum route, with physical controls for reading and removing the gold emphasis. The next hall compares measured angles on a plane, a sphere and a Poincare disk. Its former seven-value curvature dial concealed only three geometries; the revised encounter names those three models and measures their corners correctly. All existing artifact families remain. Russell now asks for an answer before explaining the contradiction. An existing workbench returns with physical IN / OUT buttons and a finite separation comparison. Godel keeps its mature manuscript; its two principal exhibits now identify their animations as illustrations. Escher now lets the visitor follow a marker, measure tread heights and compare five constructions. Its triangle aligns separated endpoints to a marked camera position. All four artifact families remain; the manuscript distinguishes a persuasive image from a spatial connection and a geometric measurement from a theorem. Brouwer now begins with actual visitor choices. Its existing Cantor workbench becomes a third primary, supplying a finite witness the reader can check. Eight artifact families remain, the authored placements reach the museum, and the chapter distinguishes construction, illustration and proof. Florensky now has an authored hall: independently controlled reports share a full-size threshold, followed by a sphere that keeps both readings. Both quantum visual toys remain as comparisons, with their limits made explicit. All eight declared halls are now authored; Crisis Synthesis remains the next review pass.

items.title: A statement becomes something we can ask again
items.description: The plaque now offers NEXT and GOLD at 1.05 m. Its colonnade and supporting artifacts return, repositioned around the central walk. The printed-angle triangle becomes a primary comparison: the next hall measures what this one labels. No secondary artifact is removed.

The fifth postulate, with NEXT and GOLD below the plaque.

items.before: So let's break the branch. `highlight_fifth` is an exported bool. Set it false and the fifth reads in the same warm grey as the rest, and `parallel_highlighted` never fires — the branch that shouted was the branch that coloured. `postulate_selected` still emits at index four, the way it does at every other. Cycle again and ask whether the fifth still feels like the odd one.
items.after: Now press GOLD. It switches `highlight_fifth` off: the fifth reads in the same warm grey as the rest, and `parallel_highlighted` never fires — the branch that shouted was the branch that coloured. `postulate_selected` still emits at index four, the way it does at every other. Cycle again and ask whether the fifth still feels like the odd one.

items.title: Three hosts; three measurements
items.description: HOST selects plane, sphere or disk. The surface sits behind the console and tilts towards the visitor so the controls do not cover its triangle. The displayed angles come from analytic edge tangents. Independent spherical and hyperbolic formulas agree with these example sums: 180.0, 202.1 and 103.1 degrees. The bench illustrates a relation; it does not independently verify a curvature integral or prove Gauss–Bonnet.
captions: PLANE · straight segments, 180.0 degrees.
SPHERE · great-circle edges, 202.1 degrees.
DISK · hyperbolic geodesics, 103.1 degrees.
items.image_note: Three states of the revised workbench in the actual museum, from the same camera at 1.70 m. These are separate example triangles, not an unchanged triangle transported between spaces. The collision-test walker is hidden for photographs.
items.before: The previous room let you stand inside an assumption until it stopped feeling like one. This room puts the assumption on a dial. There is a slider here with a number on it, and the number is the curvature of space — negative to the left, zero in the middle, positive to the right. Flatness is the detent at zero. It is not the centre because it is correct; it is the centre because it is zero.
items.after:
Start with PLANE at the bench near the entrance. Follow each yellow edge with your eye. Before moving the slider, predict what will happen to the angle sum when the triangle sits on a sphere. More than 180°? Less? The same, because it is still a triangle?

Move to SPHERE. The edges take the short great-circle routes between their endpoints. Look at a corner: each incoming direction has to be read on the sphere, where the corner lives. The total rises. Move back to PLANE. It returns to 180°.

Now try DISK. The triangle lies inside a circle; its sides curve towards the centre. Its angles add to less than 180°. The disk looks flat. That is already a complication worth staying with.
items.report_label: Control signals and independent angle checks

items.title: Keep the invitation; distinguish what each artifact can establish
items.description: Bowing a line in a flat plane is separated from changing its host geometry. Unequal gaps between three parallels are separated from failure of parallelism. The Riemann sphere remains primary, and all six non-Euclidean exhibits remain available. The revised chapter distinguishes a visible disk boundary, metric distance and the point added at infinity.
items.before: Geometry was chosen, not found. That is settled by the time you leave this room, and it is settled without anyone having to be wrong.
items.after:
Mathematics lets us specify different geometries. Which geometry models a physical situation is a further question, answered with measurements and assumptions; a slider cannot settle it. Nor does one curvature value specify every possible space.

Here the question is close enough to touch. When we change the host, what must a line do to remain straight? What have we kept, and what have we quietly replaced?

For now, return the slider to PLANE. The floor has not moved. Your account of it has.
items.report_label: Decisions, remaining six halls and verification limits

items.title: IN. OUT. It looks like enough choice.
items.description: A previously existing workbench joins the six earlier artifact families. Test both membership answers, then change the domain. The lamp accepts OUT in the finite restricted example. The hotel becomes primary again because it supplies a surprise with a constructive answer. A reserved centre passage keeps decorative plinths out of the walk.
captions: Unrestricted rule: IN requires OUT. Trying OUT also contradicts the rule.
Within an existing set U: OUT agrees. The four numbered dots are the finite ordinal example.
items.image_note: Two states of the current workbench inside the actual museum, with the same camera at 1.65 m. These are not before/after software versions. The test walker is hidden for photographs; museum artifacts remain visible. Physical button signals and selected collision-body walks pass; tracked hands and headset reading remain untested.
items.before: Four objects arranged as a cross, with a box at the centre, and every one of them is the same sentence said in a different material.
items.after: A rule stands at the entrance, with two buttons beneath it. IN. OUT. It looks like enough choice.
items.report_label: Exact Russell manuscript diff; Godel unchanged

items.title: Keep the objects. Ask what each one can establish.
items.description: The box remains an image of regress; the workbench supplies the two-case contradiction. The liar introduces truth rather than membership. Nested braces do not prove self-membership. The hotel supplies a valid reassignment. The revised text keeps these encounters and removes the claim that they are all the same contradiction.
captions: The membership bench faces the entrance, with the earlier artifacts around and beyond it.
items.image_note: Current Godot museum capture. A side approach and central passage were checked separately with the museum collision body. This is not a complete continuous headset route test.
items.before: That is the difference this room needs you to hold. The hotel is a **surprise**, and it settles. The box, the barber, the liar and the brace are **contradictions**, and they do not. One of them is your intuition being wrong about infinity; the other four are a formal system being unable to say what it just said. Standing beside each other, they mark the line the rest of the chapter walks along.
items.after: Keep this surprise close to the contradiction. An offended expectation is not yet an inconsistency. Sometimes the answer requires a construction we had not imagined. Sometimes the requested construction cannot satisfy its own terms.

items.title: Godel: let the existing text set the standard
items.description: The short chapter already distinguishes a failed search, a broken search and a theorem about proof. Its text and map are byte-preserved. The sentence machine now says ILLUSTRATION — NOT PROOF SEARCH, and the sorter states that its areas and tokens do not count truths. Source and registry descriptions state the mathematical assumptions. No proof-search implementation is claimed.
captions: The sentence machine, with its new illustration label.
The sorter: an illustrated relation, with destinations chosen in advance.
items.image_note: Current Godot museum captures. Both exhibits instantiate; these views do not certify access to every exhibit or continuous navigation of Godel’s hall. Its existing placement over gaps remains a later spatial review item.

items.title: Escher: where does the rise return?
items.description: Physical STEP, BACK, FORM and RESET controls expose the existing staircase constructions. The light follows the selected tread. A side readout measures the displayed tread centres. The closed circuit gains and loses the same height; the open run stops at its cut end. The visitor stays on the floor.
captions: RETURN SIDE, after a circuit: 0.88 m up and 0.88 m down.
OPEN RUN: the marker stops at the cut end, 0.79 m above its start.
items.image_note: Current Godot museum captures from the same camera at 1.70 m. Two settings of one artifact, not before/after software versions. The visible light, readout and physical button signals were checked. Tracked-hand use and headset legibility remain unverified.
items.text_kind: book — an encounter replaces an unsupported promise
items.before: Check any corner of it. The riser is a sensible height, the tread is level, the joint between this flight and the next is square. Check the next corner and the same is true. Walk the whole loop checking as you go, approve every junction individually, and you will arrive back at the step you began on having climbed the entire way. Nothing you inspected was wrong. The object cannot exist.
items.after: Follow it around the corners. Before completing the circuit, predict where the height will be given back. Then finish. The marker is at the start. The upward and downward totals agree.

items.title: The body can leave the assigned viewpoint
items.description: The triangle had a depth gap, but its marked viewpoint did not align the ends and its detector had no active-camera caller. The back endpoint now lies on the correct viewing ray; optional camera tracking updates the alignment feedback. The chapter calls this a perspective study and does not claim it reproduces the complete Penrose tribar.
captions: At the marked eye position: top endpoint centres project together.
Camera shifted 0.55 m sideways: the separation becomes visible.
items.image_note: Current single-camera Godot captures of the same unmoved artifact. Endpoint projection was independently checked with Camera3D.unproject_position. Beam thickness is still visible. These photographs do not establish the same illusion for two eyes in a headset.
items.text_kind: book — a connection in the image
items.before: Which reframes the staircase too. Consistency here is not a property the object has. It is a property of a *view* of the object, and the view is a position you can be standing in without knowing you chose it.
items.after: The mark offers a place from which to believe the image. You are allowed to leave it. What else becomes convincing only when we remain in the assigned place?
items.report_label: Controls, visible marker, height and projection checks

items.title: Keep the comparison; make the claim testable
items.description: The pipe stays beside the first experiment and the trident remains at the rear. Two rods becoming three tines does not alone establish impossibility: the reader is invited to follow an edge. The book, wall speech, registry descriptions and current encounter hashes agree. Other Foundations manuscripts and maps are byte-preserved.
captions: The entrance study and pipe, with the other comparisons beyond.
CLOSING DROP: the extra dark tread marks a continued rise; the marker returns to the actual first tread.
items.image_note: Current Godot museum views. Five selected collision-body approaches pass. They do not constitute a continuous route test or learner verification. No live museum restart or bake replacement was performed.
items.before: Consistency is not compositional. You can verify every step and learn nothing about the loop, and this is not a limitation of care or of time — it is a fact about what local verification is. The information that the staircase does not close is not present at any junction. It appears only in the sum.
items.after: Recognition is generous. It supplies stairs we want to climb and connections we expect to continue. This hall asks us to keep that generosity while also approaching, counting, changing position. The pleasure of the impossible image survives finding how a particular model was made.
items.report_label: Decisions, preserved work and remaining limits

items.title: Brouwer: the clock is no longer the author
items.description: The old dots were fixed: time made them bob but did not choose a term. The opt-in bench now records exactly what the visitor presses. CHOOSE 0, CHOOSE 1 and RESET replace an absent interaction with an encounter the chapter can follow. The next value remains unchosen.
captions: No terms chosen. Waiting leaves the row empty.
Five button presses: 0, 1, 1, 0, 1. The next term waits.
items.image_note: Current Godot museum captures from the same camera at 1.65 m. Two states of the revised bench, not before/after software images. Button signals are exercised; tracked hands and headset reading are not yet tested.
items.text_kind: book — give the reader the choice the earlier text could only discuss
items.before: I would not repair that by wiring buttons to everything. The gap is more useful named than closed, because it is the actual condition the philosophy describes: the construction is *possible*, nobody has performed it, and on Brouwer's own terms that means it does not yet exist. The room is in the state it is teaching.
items.after: And who chose the things you are allowed to choose? There are two buttons. You may make a rhythm, break it, repeat yourself, refuse to continue. The freedom has a shape before your hand arrives.

items.title: Invite the existing artifact that supplies the evidence
items.description: Cantor is promoted from secondary to primary. Its gold diagonal and red constructed string make disagreement inspectable, while the first bench supplies a contrast between chosen and rule-driven continuation. A lateral monitor position exposes the red row that the console previously obscured.
captions: Four rows of four bits. The red string disagrees with each row at its diagonal bit.
Sixteen rows of sixteen bits. Earlier bits persist as the display grows.
items.image_note: Current Godot captures at N=4 and N=16. The instrument displays finite bit strings, not complete real numbers or a completed infinity. Model assertions checked all five supported sizes; see the report for the standalone-runner shutdown limitation.
items.text_kind: book — a finite construction supports a carefully scoped argument
items.before: Cantor's diagonal argument is often taught as a proof by contradiction — assume the reals are listable, derive absurdity — but it does not have to be, and this bench does not present it that way. Turn the slider, the list grows, the diagonal extends, and a number is *built*, digit by digit, that differs from the first entry in the first place, the second in the second, and so on. At the end you are holding the witness. It is not that a missing real must exist; it is that here it is, and you watched it being made.
items.after: This is a finite stage of diagonalisation. The mathematical argument for infinite binary sequences applies the same rule to every row of a proposed countable list. The headset displays finite strings, up to 32 bits here. Their disagreement is real and inspectable; displaying it does not display the completed infinite object.

items.title: Eight works, three primaries, one comparison that can be walked
items.description: The earlier museum placement setting hid four of the eight map artifacts. The hall now follows the map, with the choice bench at the entrance and comparison bays along a clear aisle. Optional template piers and the entry gate are omitted here. The excluded-middle caption no longer describes an unproved claim as a third truth value; the staircase is labelled as a timed model.
captions: Existing witness, diagonal, logic, staircase and geometric comparisons remain in the hall.
items.image_note: Five selected collision-body walks pass, including the aisle beside the first bench. This is controlled museum evidence, not a continuous headset playthrough. No live museum restart or bake replacement was performed.
items.text_kind: book — compare what is produced with what its caption claims
items.before: In a room about constructive proof, that is the entire lesson standing in the corner. Both objects state a result. Neither exhibits a witness. Both are, on the strict reading this room is teaching, claims for which no construction has been performed — and both are perfectly convincing to look at, which is the danger Brouwer was pointing at.
items.after: The triangle and parallel lines return from the earlier geometry. Someone has already supplied their coordinates and relations. A preset is still a construction. What it may conceal is the work by which its particular case supports—or fails to support—a general claim. Look at the displayed shape and ask what the caption adds beyond it.

items.title: Florensky: the doorway becomes an encounter
items.description: The manuscript promised a walkable door, but the earlier artifact was under a metre high and this map was absent from the authored museum route. A full-size frame now holds two ghost leaves. OPEN, CLOSED and CLEAR buttons let the visitor change independent reports while the passage remains open. The original small illustration remains available outside this opt-in study.
captions: Both reports are present. The closed leaf is visible; the passage is open.
Only the open report remains. The same frame and camera.
items.image_note: Two states of the revised Godot museum encounter, not before/after software versions. Button signals are exercised through the existing interaction component. Tracked hands and headset reading remain untested.
items.text_kind: book — begin with a passage the reader can test
items.before: The gate makes it a thing you walk through. Both leaves are real, the frame holds them, and the room around it is not on fire. That is the entire claim, and the reason it needs to be a body rather than a sentence is that the sentence sounds like a trick and the door does not.
items.after: And your passage? The engine gives collision to the frame, but not to the ghost leaves. The visible assertion “closed” has no authority to stop you. Someone had to make that decision. A system can preserve conflicting descriptions and still have to decide who gets through.

items.title: Keep the contradiction local; keep the claims precise
items.description: The console stores support for two opposed reports. Their coexistence supplies no support for an unrelated alarm claim. This is a finite information model, not a complete logical calculus. The sphere holds A AND not-A without the old observation-collapse or BOTH/NEITHER flicker. The chapter distinguishes paraconsistency, dialetheism and Florensky-inspired antinomy.
captions: The report console. NO SUPPORT does not mean the alarm has been proved silent.
The colour changes; both readings remain. Plain words avoid a missing conjunction glyph in the baked font.
items.image_note: Actual Godot captures. The console text is fixed to its casing so it no longer clips when viewed from an angle. The sphere remains a visual study; rendering both faces of a mesh is not a proof of a true contradiction.
items.text_kind: book — let the unresolved account lead to a bodily question
items.before: Read the parameter carefully, because the ordering is the argument. BOTH is where the object rests. Looking at it can knock it briefly to one side, and it returns. This is the inverse of the arrangement you would expect and the inverse of the two objects across the room: the single-valued states are the transient ones, and the contradiction is the stable configuration.
items.after: There is a desire here to inhabit something before its description has settled. A body can outgrow the terms supplied for it. It need not become a logical contradiction to deserve more room. The question returns to the doorway: must every account agree before a passage can be allowed?

items.title: Four works remain; resemblance becomes a question
items.description: The Schrödinger box and superposition display remain secondary comparisons at the back. Their captions and lookup descriptions now identify a random-outcome toy and an opacity animation. The display has no measurement operation. The chapter no longer calls quantum superposition a logical contradiction with an expiry. An automatic statue that blocked the exit approach is excluded in this hall.
captions: The retained quantum pair, on either side of the rear approach.
items.image_note: Six selected collision-body walks and 24 behavior/geometry assertions pass in the actual museum probe; process exit 0. This does not certify continuous museum travel, tracked-hand operation or learner understanding. No live museum restart or bake replacement was performed.
items.text_kind: book — distinguish concepts without discarding their visual relation
items.before: The cat is both alive and dead until observed — and then it is not. Observation collapses the superposition to one branch and the other is gone. The display says the same thing about a qubit: `|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩`, genuinely occupying both, and genuinely resolving to one when measured. Both are contradictions *with an expiry*. The world tolerates them precisely because looking ends them.
items.after: Quantum superposition describes a state in relation to a basis; it is not simply the logical assertion P and not-P.[^3] These objects cannot lend physics as a certificate for the sphere. They can help us notice how readily a shared visual language—two colours, a sealed box, a change when watched—makes different problems seem identical.

items.title: Next: Crisis Synthesis
items.description: All eight Foundations Crisis halls are now authored. The synthesis still needs a focused review: bring these different responses together without treating incompleteness, construction, antinomy and quantum superposition as the same gap. Earlier supporting critical prose and the box’s missing tracked-hand opening remain named follow-ups.
